name: SpinQuant: LLM Quantization with Learned Rotations
problem: Random rotations remove activation outliers (QuaRot) but the quality you get depends heavily on WHICH random rotation you draw - some draws are far better than others.
mechanism: Same computational-invariance trick as QuaRot, but the rotation is LEARNED rather than drawn at random. Searches over rotation parameterizations (Cayley-optimized orthogonal transform on the GPU/Stiefel manifold) that are identity-equivalent at full precision, optimized with gradient descent on the quantization-aware objective so as to minimize downstream quantized accuracy loss. Also introduces CPTQ (progressive end-to-end weight quantization from 16-bit down to the target width).
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract, W4 weights + activations + KV cache): narrows the zero-shot reasoning accuracy gap to full precision to 2.9 points on LLaMA-2 7B, surpassing LLM-QAT by 19.1 points and SmoothQuant by 25.0 points at the same precision; on hard-to-quantize LLaMA-3 8B it cuts the gap to full precision by up to 45.1% relative to QuaRot. COMPRESSION RATIO: 4-bit on weights, activations and KV cache (~4x each vs FP16). QUALITY COST: 2.9 points of zero-shot accuracy - the best number in the 4-bit PTQ literature at the time, and still a 2.9-point regression. Also reports up to a 13-point spread between good and bad random rotations, which is the paper's real argument.
